name: Choline

track.title: Pilot in people
track.line: No energy or fat-loss injection studies found

track.title: FDA approval
track.line: Only radioactive Choline C 11, a PET scan agent

what.text: Choline is a nutrient the body uses to make cell membranes and the nerve messenger acetylcholine. It is the “C” in “MIC” injections, usually as choline chloride.

src.label: PubChem (NIH National Library of Medicine), choline record

research.text: We found no published human study of injected choline, alone or in MIC blends, for energy or fat loss.

us.text: No FDA-approved choline product is for energy or weight loss. Using choline injections for those uses is not an approved use.

The only FDA-approved injected choline products we found are Choline C 11, a radioactive tracer first approved in 2012 for PET scans in men with suspected prostate cancer recurrence. Other approved drugs use choline only as a salt partner (for example choline fenofibrate).

us.text: FDA lists choline chloride as nominated for compounding and “under evaluation” (Category 1) for both pharmacy compounding (503A) and outsourcing facilities (503B).

src.label: FDA, Bulk drug substances nominated under section 503A (categories)
FDA, Bulk drug substances nominated under section 503B (categories)

us.text: Compounded drugs are not FDA approved. That includes compounded MIC and lipotropic injection blends containing choline.

src.label: FDA, Compounding and the FDA: Q&A

us.text: FDA’s recall records list many compounded “lipotropic”, “Lipo-B” and methionine/inositol/choline (MIC) injections recalled by compounding pharmacies, most often for “lack of assurance of sterility.” Examples: Isomeric Pharmacy Solutions’ cyanocobalamin/methionine/inositol/choline vials (2017), Partell Specialty Pharmacy’s MIC + B12 vials (2018), Assurance Infusion’s Lipo B vials (2020) and Tailor Made Compounding’s MIC + B12 + carnitine vials (2022). These were recalls of specific pharmacies’ lots, not a ruling on the ingredients.

world.lead: We found no approved choline medicine for energy or weight in the US or on EMA’s central list. Other countries were not checked.

countries.status: Not approved for energy or weight loss (only Choline C 11, a PET scan agent, is approved). Compounded MIC blends are not FDA approved.

after.text: EMA’s list of centrally authorised medicines has no choline product for energy or weight; choline appears only as part of unrelated medicines. We did not check national EU authorisations.

after.title: Sport
after.text: Choline is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List or on the 2027 List, which takes effect January 1, 2027. Separately, the lists' method M2.2 bans intravenous infusions or injections of more than 100 mL per 12-hour period, except in hospital treatment, surgery or clinical tests.

side.text: There is no FDA label for injected choline chloride, so there is no labelled side-effect list.
FDA’s recall records show compounded MIC injections recalled for lack of assurance of sterility, a risk with any injection made without sterile controls.

unconfirmed: Canada, UK (MHRA), national EU and Australian (TGA) status could not be confirmed from the regulators’ records.
A 2021 FDA advisory committee review of choline chloride for the 503A list could not be opened, so it is left out.
surprises: MIC injections are marketed for fat loss, yet we found no human study of injected choline for that use; the only FDA-approved injected choline is a radioactive scan agent.
